Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:89: Further, purity is found concerning the heart, "create in me a pure heart, O God" (Psalms 51:12) - and this is the essential point relevant to our subject of cleaving: for if the heart is pure, all the limbs are pure, as they explained, of blessed memory, in Midrash Shocher Tov (Midrash Tehillim, Psalm 14 [sic]), in these words: "I, the LORD, search the heart, I test the kidneys" (Jeremiah 17:10) - why does He mention the heart and the kidneys more than all the other limbs? Rather, the eyes follow the heart, and the 248 limbs follow the heart, and since the kidneys give counsel and the heart decides, therefore He mentions only these, and the Holy One, blessed be He, examines them. And so it says (1 Chronicles 28:9), "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him, for the LORD searches all hearts" - these are the two hearts, the good inclination and the evil inclination. A parable of an architect who built the city with rooms, sewers, and caves; after some time he became a tax collector, and the people of the city began hiding from him inside the rooms and the caves. He said to them, fools, why do you hide? Am I not the one who built this city? I am the one who built the caves and the rooms! So too (Isaiah 29:15), "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the LORD" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:90: And in the Gate of Fear, chapter 7, we copied a similar parable - however, that parable was said concerning one who transgresses in secret, whereas here it is expounded concerning one who thinks thoughts in his heart, as it says, "woe to those who go deep to hide their counsel from the LORD" - and the rooms and caves mentioned in the discourse are the chambers of the heart and the kidneys.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:91: And when a person contemplates this matter, his thought is purified - for the Name created him, and created his heart and his kidneys, and He knows his hidden depths, and before Him all is revealed, darkness like light, and he stands before Him always - and how could he not be ashamed to think a thing not according to His will?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:92: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, further explained in Bereshit Rabbah on the verse (Jeremiah 32:19), "great in counsel," and so on, in these words: "great" - "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth by Your great power and Your outstretched arm; nothing is too wonderful for You" (ibid. 32:17). Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah: what is "behold, You have made the heavens and the earth"? From that time, nothing is too wonderful for You. Rabbi Chagai in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak (1 Chronicles 28:9): "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the LORD searches all hearts and understands every imagination of the thoughts" - even before the thought is completed in a person's heart, it is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak said: even before a creature is formed, its thought is already revealed before Him. Rabbi Yudan said of himself (Psalms 139:4), "for there is not a word on my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, You know it altogether" - even before my tongue is engaged, lo, O LORD, You know it all - to this point. And behold, from the plain sense of his words there is proof for our intent, without our elaborating on it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:93: And when a person contemplates that the Shechinah is above his head, it is fitting that he purify his brain and his heart, so that the Shechinah find a place in which to rest - for these are the two primary limbs of a person, in which the essence of vitality depends, and therefore he must purify them from every blemish that blemishes them, for a small thing will blemish them because of their extreme subtlety and spirituality, since they allude to a supernal place in Atzilut, as explained in the Tikkunim (Introduction, page 17a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:94: And corresponding to the purity of thought, King David, peace be upon him, said elsewhere (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart." I have already explained "clean hands" above, and copied the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, concerning cleanliness. And afterward he says "and a pure heart" - in this manner, that he not draw his will and his heart to the Other Side, but rather draw them after the service of the Holy One, blessed be He. "Who has not lifted up his soul to vanity" - "nafsho" [his soul] is written but read "nafshi" [my soul] - and they have already established: "nafshi" is the soul of David, the side of faith; "nafsho" is literally a person's own soul - because when his soul departs this world, it ascends through the worthy deeds it performed in the world, to go among all those [worthy ones], along the lines of (Psalms 116:9), "I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living" - and because he did not lift up his soul to vanity, "he shall receive blessing from the LORD," and so on - to this point. Behold, it is explained in this discourse the virtue of one who repairs his deeds and his thoughts for the service of his Owner, because his soul is part of the Shechinah - this is "nafsho" and "nafshi," and all is one - and according to the repair of his soul, he repairs above, and therefore he will merit what King David, peace be upon him, said, "I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living," and "he shall receive blessing from the LORD," namely the Shechinah, as is known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:95: And from the affirmative you infer the negative: one who lifts up his soul to vanity and defiles his thought blemishes, Heaven forfend, above, and his soul shall not ascend to the mountain of the LORD nor to His holy place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:96: And behold, one must purify the heart from envy, hatred, rivalry, and all the evil attributes that depend on the heart, such as worry, sighing, sadness, anger, mockery, and the like - and when the heart is empty of all this, it is a fitting dwelling for the Shechinah, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 6, page 22b), that a person must repair a fitting dwelling for the Shechinah in his heart, namely through the repair explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:97: And further they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 29, end of page 72), that a person's inside must match his outside. He said there that the wine, which is the Torah, must be guarded and sealed in a good jar, and he said the jar is the heart - and if this jar has been poured with the wine of the evil inclination, it needs rinsing three times, and needs rinsing and washing like the cup of blessing, meaning that his inside matches his outside; and in these words: and when this jar, which is a pure heart within and without, [is fit], wisdom dwells there, of which it is said (Proverbs 8:22), "the LORD possessed me [kanani] at the beginning of His way" - "kanani" is certainly "kankan" [jar]; and if this jar is pure, it is said of it, "and be innocent" [ve-nakeh]; and if not, "whoever touches it shall not go unpunished [lo yinakeh]" (ibid. 6:29) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:98: And so too the matter of the purity of thought: for the brain is an important vessel, more subtle than the heart, and therefore it is in the head; and you know, concerning tefillin, that one does not lower [an object] from greater holiness to lesser holiness - namely, [one does not take] the strap of the head-tefillin to make it into that of the hand-tefillin, even though the passages written in the head are the same as those in the hand - rather, since they were placed in the head, they acquired greater virtue and spirituality, and one must not lower them to make them into the hand-tefillin. Therefore one must purify his thought all the more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:99: And whoever merits to purify his thought will merit, in the future, what they said, of blessed memory (Berachot 17a): the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads. And they merit the crown upon the head only because they purified the brain in their heads, so that the Shechinah would crown herself upon them - and in the future too they merit this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:100: And it appears that the secret of "their crowns upon their heads" is what is said of Joshua the High Priest (Zechariah 3:5), "and they set a pure mitre upon his head" - and it says "a pure mitre" because the crown was made for him not merely [as an ordinary crown], but because he purified his thought, as explained. And it is possible to say - and this appears to be the essential meaning - that the pure mitre was made for him from the commandments dependent on the head, such as donning tefillin, the spreading of tzitzit over one's head, and the commandment of the corners of the head [pe'ot]; and likewise the purity of thought through the pure intentions by which a person unifies himself to his Owner.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:101: And concerning the matter of purity, we find in the Zohar and the Ra'aya Meheimna places that differ from one another - in Parashat Korach (page 176a), and also in Parashat Chukat (page 180b), it is explained that the priest is "holy" and the Levite is "pure," and therefore the [red] heifer, which is from the side of the left, comes to purify and not to sanctify, for the essence of purity is on the left. But in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ekev, page 273b), that purity is on the right and holiness on the left.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:102: And concerning holiness, it will be explained further on, with God's help. However, concerning purity, it appears to me that there are two kinds of purity: the first is purity through water, as explained above, and water is known to be from the side of Chesed. And there is a purity from the side of the left, as it is written (Numbers 31:23), "every thing that may abide the fire, you shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:103: And so vessels are purified in two ways: with water, namely immersion for eating vessels that have not been used with fire, or purification by fire if they were used with fire - as Scripture says, "every thing that may abide the fire, you shall make it go through the fire, and it shall be pure," and so on, "whatever may not abide the fire you shall make go through the water."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:104: And so too concerning the purification of souls from their blemish - according to the blemish is the purification required - namely, the four categories of atonement that Rabbi Yishmael would expound (Yoma 86a): if a person transgressed a positive commandment and repented, he is forgiven at once, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:22), "return, backsliding children, I will heal your backslidings." This category of atonement is from the side of Chesed, for it is known (Tikkunei Zohar 107b) that the 248 positive commandments are from the side of the right, and the negative commandments from the side of the left - and therefore, the blemish of a positive commandment, which is in Chesed, once he has repented, he is forgiven at once, meaning that the purification from the waters of Chesed purifies him, and he is forgiven at once.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:105: And the transgression of a positive commandment is when he is lazy in fulfilling the commandments - such as matzah on Passover and the like - namely, nullifying a commandment by sitting and not acting. And its remedy is alacrity from now on to fulfill what is within his power, and the water, namely the waters of the supernal atonement, will flow and wash away that blemish in the soul - for even nullifying a commandment causes a blemish in the soul, though not as great as transgressing a negative commandment - and purification in the waters of the mikveh will avail to purify what he was lazy about in the commandment. And the reason is that when a person fulfills the commandment, he draws supernal light to clothe his soul, but when he nullifies the commandment, immediately the external force is present there and rests upon him - for they are called "these" [eleh, associated with idolatry] and rest in any place empty of holiness, as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Terumah (page 128a), that they rest upon a person for free, and especially when he is idle, "like finds like" and is aroused. And therefore, in order to strip that spirit of impurity from himself, purification in the waters of the mikveh, which are from the side of Chesed, is needed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:106: And when the blemish is in a negative commandment - namely the second category of atonement: if a person transgressed a negative commandment and repents, repentance suspends [punishment] and the Day of Atonement atones, as it is said (Leviticus 16:30), "for on this day He shall atone for you, to purify you." If a person transgressed [a sin punishable by] karet or death by the court and repents, repentance and the Day of Atonement suspend, and suffering finishes the atonement, as it is said (Psalms 89:33), "then I will visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues." But one who has profaned the Name, and so on [is different]. Behold, these three categories are all, in general, negative commandments, and therefore their purification is all through the fire of Gevurah - for the fast of the Day of Atonement purifies through the affliction of the soul and the offering of one's fat and blood, melted in the fire of the affliction, as will be further explained concerning fasting: that fasting is a purifying fire against the fire of the evil inclination, along the lines of "every thing that may abide the fire"; and so suffering and plagues are all certainly purification from the side of fire - and needless to say the day of death. And the nature of fire is to refine both inside and out - along the lines of the blemish that boiled itself in the fire of the evil inclination, so purification and refinement are needed - and therefore the essence of purification is through fire, along the lines of (Pesachim, chapter 2, mishnah 1), "there is no removal of chametz except by burning." And therefore fasting is efficacious for a penitent to purify and refine him inside and out, and likewise the wearing of sackcloth on his flesh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:107: And in the Torah both of these purifications are found, and therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that the Torah is likened to fire, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:29), "is not My word like fire," and is likened to water, as it is said (Isaiah 55:1), "ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters" - and the reason is that the Torah is the secret of the middle line, so it is fitting that everything be included within it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:108: And all the particular aspects explained are all found in the Torah - whether to strip the spirit of impurity, or to cool the impurity from the fire of the evil inclination, or to refine the evil inclination - and therefore it is written of it (Psalms 12:7), "the words of the LORD are pure words."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:109: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 80b), that the essence of purification is through Torah, in these words: come and see, a person is never purified except through the words of Torah - therefore words of Torah do not receive impurity, because it stands to purify these impure ones, and healing is found in the Torah, as it is written (Proverbs 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel, and marrow to your bones," and it is written (ibid. 10:27), "the fear of the LORD adds days." Purity is found in the Torah, as it is written (Psalms 19:10), "the fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever" - what is "enduring forever"? That it stands constantly in that purity and never departs from it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:110: And the essence of the purification of thought is through the occupation with Torah, as they said, of blessed memory (Kiddushin 30b): I created the evil inclination, I created for it the Torah as its antidote. And Maimonides wrote at the end of the Laws of Forbidden Relations, in these words: more than all this, they said, one should turn himself and his thought to words of Torah and broaden his mind with wisdom, for thoughts of forbidden relations gain strength only in a heart empty of wisdom - and concerning wisdom it says (Proverbs 5:19), "a loving hind and a graceful doe," and so on. And therefore we placed, in the matter of purity, the purity of Torah last, because it rises above all and is the essence of all purifications: "purity brings one to holiness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:111: And Ra'avad explained, in the Gate of Holiness, the matter of "purity brings one to holiness," and began the gate with the verse (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and he said, relevant to our subject, in these words: I shall first explain what the two holinesses mentioned in this verse are; and likewise what they said in the beraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, "purity brings one to holiness" - I shall explain what purity is and what holiness is, and from this you will know what the two holinesses are.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:112: And he says first, that impurities are of two kinds: those found by touch, and those not by touch. By touch - such as touching carcasses and their being moved, touching creeping things, the lying and sitting [defilement] of a zav, a zavah, and a leper, the sighting of a seminal emission, and the impurity of the dead. And likewise one who transgresses sins, such as one who has relations with forbidden relatives, and one who eats forbidden things - these are impurities that are by touch, for one who has relations with forbidden relatives and one who eats forbidden things is called impure, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 18:24), "do not defile yourselves with any of these," and "and you shall be defiled by them" (ibid. 11:43). And the impurity that is not by touch - such as the seeing of the eyes, the hearing of the ears, and the utterance of the lips, in a matter that is not fitting to see, nor to hear, nor to speak of - and the contemplation of the heart in matters that are forbidden.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:113: Purity too is found by touch and not by touch. For the purification of touchings and movings, and of seminal emission, and of plagues, and of the impurity of the dead, is through immersions and sprinklings, and other matters explained concerning the leper - and this is purity by touch. And the purity that is not by touch is separation from sin and forbidden things, and the cleanliness of the heart, the thought, and the tongue, and the closing of the eyes and the stopping of the ears from seeing and hearing evil - all these are called pure, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "from all your sins before the LORD you shall be pure," and it is written (Ezekiel 36:25), "from all your impurities and from all your idols I will purify you," and it is written (Isaiah 33:15), "and shuts his eyes from seeing evil," and so on, and it is written (Proverbs 22:11), "he who loves purity of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend," and it is written (Psalms 24:4), "clean hands and a pure heart" - and if he is careful of these he is called pure, and whoever is not careful is called impure; and one who speaks things unfitting for him is called impure of lips, and one careful of this is called pure of lips.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:114: It follows that impurity is of two kinds and purity of two kinds - except that there is a distinction between separating from the impurity of sins and forbidden things and separating from other impurities. For one who separates from touchings and other similar impurities is called only "pure," as it is written (Leviticus 14:8), "and he shall wash in water, and be pure." But one who separates from sins and forbidden things is called both pure and holy - pure, as we have said, and holy, as it is written in the passage of forbidden relations (Leviticus 20:7), "sanctify yourselves and be holy," and also in the passage of creeping things it is written (ibid. 11:44), "sanctify yourselves and be holy." And not only that, but the other impurities do not involve the impurity of thought, but with the impurity of sins and forbidden things, just as one must separate from the sinful act itself, so must he separate from thinking of it, that he not contemplate the sin in his heart - and if a thought about them comes to him, he must force himself and remove it from his heart, all the more so that he not intend to complete it in his heart. And since a completed thought is what leads to the deed and is considered as a deed - concerning this it is said (Ezekiel 14:5), "in order to take hold of the house of Israel by their heart" - and this is the second holiness that Scripture warns of: "sanctify yourselves" through deed, "and be holy" through thought. Do you not see what is written at the end of the verse, "for I am holy" - just as I am holy in deed and in thought, so shall you be holy - from this you learn that a person is not called holy until he is sanctified in deed and in thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:115: And now you shall understand and know that a person cannot attain this attribute until he sets aside, of what is permitted to him, some portion, and fences himself with a fence around things that are permitted, which are the way and path that lead to habituating oneself in sin - along the lines of what they said (Niddah 13b), whoever puts his hand below his navel, his hand should be cut off; and as they said (ibid.), whoever holds his member and urinates is as though he brought a flood upon the world; and as Rabbi Yosi said (Shabbat 118b), I have never in my life gazed at my own circumcised member - and they asked, if so, why did they call him "our holy Rabbi"? They answered, he had an extra measure of holiness in that he never put his hand beneath his belt. And all this separation was a fence, so that the desire of forbidden relations not attach to him - for the evil inclination quarrels with a person and accuses him, to entice and seduce him, and this is its way: it entices him to sate his soul and fulfill all his desires with everything permitted to him; and after it has taught him to fulfill all his desires with the hunger of his soul, when his hand does not find what is permitted to him, it will entice him to fulfill his desires from the forbidden, easily - and from the light [prohibition] to the severe, and from the severe to one more severe still, until it says to him, go and worship idols and deny Him who spoke and the world came into being, that there is no judgment and no judge, no Garden of Eden and no Gehinnom and no other world. And so the wise man said in the book of Ecclesiastes (cf. Ecclesiastes 9:3), "this is an evil among all that is done under the sun," and so on, "for the living know that they shall die," and so on, "go, eat your bread with joy," and so on, "enjoy life with the wife whom you love," and so on - all these are the words of the evil inclination - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:116: We shall not elaborate further on the explanation of the verse as he, of blessed memory, explained it, so as not to lengthen; and he said afterward: and therefore one must strengthen and fortify himself and stand firm to fight his desires, so that he have a virtue in his soul over the soul of the beast, which has no restraint from whatever it can attain for its desire - for the desire that overpowers a person is from the power of the vegetative soul, which is the animal [soul], and therefore the wicked, who follow after their desires, are likened to beasts, as Scripture says (cf. Psalms 49:13), "man in his glory abides not," and so on, and the wise man said (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth" - "the spirit of man" refers to the soul of the righteous, which ascends upward, and "the spirit of the beast that goes downward" refers to the soul of the wicked, who are likened to a beast.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:117: And the meaning of these words is this: he said, above this (verse 20), "all go to one place; all were from the dust, and all return to the dust," and so on - meaning, there is no difference in death between the righteous and the wicked, nor even between man and beast, for all shall die and return to the dust, and among all the living there is none who can discern any distinction between one and another - and "who knows" concerning the level of the souls, whether the soul of a righteous man ascends upward and the soul of a wicked man descends downward to the earth - meaning, below the earth, which is the depths of Sheol - among all the living there is none who can discern that distinction, except the Creator alone. And this matter is known through wisdom to the wise, the masters of contemplation, but there is no known proof of it from the matter of life and death, for all are equal in this - and therefore he says "who knows," meaning, who can discern their level? For were the distinction demonstrable, the wise and the foolish alike would know it - but there is no sign or proof of it in life and in death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:118: And behold, though all souls are equal, in their death they return to the place of their desire and their striving in their lifetime - for the soul of the righteous, taken from the place of intellect, and which held fast to its intellect and its [proper] desire, returns in its death to the place of its source; but the soul of the wicked, which desired the vanities and pleasures of the world, and did not remember its origin from before, returns likewise to the place of its desire - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:119: And at the conclusion of the gate, he explained briefly the discourse we are explaining, and he said, of blessed memory: "watchfulness" is when a person is careful and guards himself before the deed comes into his hand. And "alacrity" is at the time of the deed, that he perform his commandment with alacrity, not out of laziness, and if a sin comes into his hand, he flees and separates from it with alacrity. "Cleanliness" is the cleanliness of his body and his garments from soiling, along the lines of what they said (Shabbat 114a), any Torah scholar found with a grease stain on his flesh is liable to death. "Purity" comes with regard to impurities, that he guard himself from impurities, and if he touches them, he purifies himself and eats his non-sacred food in purity. "Holiness" is the holiness of the heart and thought, as we have said. "Piety" is one who acts beyond the letter of the law in every matter, called a chassid - and all these he explains their reasoning from the verses in Shekalim - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:120: According to our approach, let us return to explain the matter of "purity brings one to holiness," and the rest of the discourse - and although above we did not explain anything concerning "separation" [perishut], because we said it is included in holiness, nevertheless, according to the wording of our version, it is fitting to explain something about it. And the matter is that holiness includes two things, as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness: the one, "turn from evil," and the second, "and do good" - and according to our version, we say that "separation" is from the aspect of "turn from evil," and "holiness" is "do good." But according to the Yerushalmi, which does not have the reading "separation," both aspects are included in holiness, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:121: And the intent of saying "purity brings one to holiness" is this: the essence of purity is the purification of each and every limb from blemish - such as the purification of the tongue from slander and other blemishing things, and the purification of the eyes from gazing at forbidden relations, and similarly for the other limbs. But holiness is a further, more inward, fence - for besides not speaking slander, he abounds in silence; and the holiness of the eye is that he not gaze beyond four cubits - as we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness concerning the holiness of each and every limb.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:122: And Ra'avad, peace be upon him, explained, in the Gate of Holiness, the matter of "holiness brings one to humility" - the matter being that when a person attains the aforementioned holiness, humility necessarily follows from it - and the reason is that the essence of holiness is a person's separation from the affairs of the world, in order to cleave to his Creator, as He says (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy" - and we elaborated in the Gate of Holiness on the explanation of this verse - see there. And since a person is cleaved to his Owner, humility necessarily follows upon him, for if they revile and disgrace him, he will not regard this world enough to respond to his disgrace, for what they say about him is a disgrace of this world, and all of it pertains to the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:123: And even if they revile him in a matter touching a blemish of the soul, the soul, being holy, does not regard the disgrace done to it, for it considers this an atonement for its iniquity, and all is a cause from Him, blessed be He, to atone for its iniquity - as King David, peace be upon him, said (2 Samuel 16:10), "the LORD has said to him, curse." And further, if they disgrace it, its Master, to whom it is attached, will regard it - and so King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 38:15), "and I was as a man who does not hear, and in whose mouth are no arguments; for in You, O LORD, do I hope; You will answer, O LORD my God." And further, a servant who stands before his master - if a man comes and disgraces him before the king, it is a disgrace for the servant to respond before his master - and for these two reasons King David, peace be upon him, said "for in You, O LORD, do I hope." And to this second reason may be attributed precisely "for in You, O LORD, do I hope" - like a servant sitting before his master who waits for his master to respond to his insult. And to the first reason it may be attributed that he said "You will answer, O LORD my God" - since You are my God, to whom my soul is cleaved, and You are my God, it is fitting for You to regard its insult.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:124: It is also possible [to understand] the attribute of humility along the lines of the attribute of humility of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him - for when Miriam and Aaron spoke about him, it is written there (Numbers 12:3), "and the man Moses was very humble." And there is an allusion to the reason for his humility in the Tikkunim (page 5b): because of the abundance of his cleaving to the Creator, he was ashamed to separate from Him and to respond, and the Name responded on his behalf. And along this path too it is possible to say that King David, peace be upon him, said, "You will answer, O LORD my God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:125: Also, the attribute of humility follows for a person through his contemplating the greatness of the Creator, which has no end or limit - as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?" - for we are not within the bounds of a creature compared to His greatness, may He be exalted - as we shall elaborate on this in the Gate of Humility, with God's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:126: And this is the inward fear explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2 - to fear His greatness. And this fear is attained only through holiness, as it is written (Psalms 34:10), "fear the LORD, His holy ones" - for if one follows the desires of the world, he has no fear at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:127: And it follows that all the levels mentioned to attain holiness are all aspects of fear, and holiness is included among them, and fear is bound to humility. And so are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Tikkunei Zohar 5b), "and humility is bound to fear," this is what is written (Proverbs 22:4), "the reward of humility is the fear of the LORD" - and we copied this discourse in the Gate of Fear, chapter 3.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:128: It follows that saying "holiness brings one to humility" is the matter of "fear brings one to humility" - and this is when a person considers, when they revile him and say everything to him, that he is not important as a creature, for one does not respond except one who considers himself something, and says, "shall one like me be reviled?" But one who considers that he is not a [significant] creature, along the lines of "and what are we?" which Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said, certainly will not respond. And further, he should consider that what is said about him is true, that it is a deficiency in the creation and existence of the world, from the side of his iniquities, such that it would have been better for him not to have been created - and he should not regard himself as having the standing of a creature, and will not come to respond at all.
